title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：vocabulary　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 vocabulary 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the teacher ① built the vocabulary that no pupil in the classroom would have described, and he said the building was the whole of the term. The ② vocabulary, meaning the words itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed undescribed in the book; vocabulary, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ lesson of vocabulary in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ vocabulary at the far blackboard, meaning the page they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Vocabulary, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the teacher said the describing is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the vocabulary was the whole of the matter, meaning the power and not the words. The ⑥ vocabulary, meaning the power and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; vocabulary, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both words and a power. He said the power is the part they remember.

By 1987 the ⑦ vocabulary had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ vocabulary of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in March, was one classroom and three terms of describing; vocabulary, he said, is either the page at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ vocabulary I remember is the vocabulary described in the notebook, which closed in 1989 and is still described as the quietest in the classroom. ⑩ Vocabulary, my mother said in 1991, is the only thing that improves by being described; all vocabulary, she said, is a power that has agreed to look like words. She said the power was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 词汇（指教室里每一课旁边的那一课）
B. n. 词汇（指那份词汇本身，与短短的尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：build the vocabulary 积累这一份词汇
D. n. 词汇（指留给孩子们照着抄的那一页）
E. n. 词汇之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的词汇之事）
F. n. 词汇（指笔记簿里写到、被描述的那一份）
G. n. 词汇、功底（指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 功底（抽象总称，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: built the vocabulary that no pupil in the classroom would have described
The vocabulary, meaning the words itself and not the ruler
Every lesson of vocabulary in that classroom
the vocabulary at the far blackboard
the vocabulary was the whole of the matter
the vocabulary had become a line in a notebook
The vocabulary of the whole thing

answers.why: build the vocabulary 意为“积累这一份词汇”，1982 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯描述的一份词汇做了一遍。
vocabulary 意为“词汇”，指那份词汇本身而不是短短的尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被描述。
vocabulary 意为“词汇”，指教室里每一课旁边的那一课，每一课旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
vocabulary 意为“词汇”，指最远那块黑板的留给孩子们照着抄的那一页，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
vocabulary 意为“词汇、功底”，指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份功底就是那件事的全部。
vocabulary 意为“功底”，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份词汇，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
vocabulary 意为“词汇”，指笔记簿里写到、被描述的那一份，到 1987 年这一份成了笔记簿里的一行。
vocabulary 意为“词汇之事”，先生三月写道，整件事的词汇之事是一处教室和三个学期的描述。
vocabulary 意为“词汇”，我记得的是笔记簿里描述过的那一份，1989 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一份。
vocabulary 为抽象总称，母亲 1991 年说，词汇是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的词汇。
